mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals a demand contraction that depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 persons for four consecutive months signals labor market strength that boosts corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically significantly different from zero in triggered periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month * 0.99 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above median in triggered periods (rank-biserial correlation < 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1% combined with a year-over-year CPI inflation above 2% for three consecutive months signals a low-rate, high-inflation regime that erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 2% from the previous quarter, accompanied by a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1%, signals a broad-based demand and supply contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ < -2% AND INDPRO monthly < previous month * 0.99
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
